name: create-implementation-plan

metadata.title: Create Implementation Plan
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Generate a detailed implementation plan document from work item details and codebase analysis, describing what to implement without code snippets, ordered by dependency layers.

output.description: Implementation plan document stored in memory with sections covering summary, prerequisites, affected files, tasks, architecture, testing, and verification

prerequisites: Work item details available in memory from fetch-work-item step
Codebase analysis available in memory from analyze-codebase step
specificActions: Follow the substeps below in sequence
Workflow: read context from memory → generate plan with all sections → store in memory → compliance check
NO CODE SNIPPETS — describe WHAT to implement, not the implementation itself
Use business-domain names, not technical/infrastructure names (e.g., 'Add account holder lookup' not 'Add GET endpoint to controller')
Order implementation tasks: dependencies/config -> module wiring -> feature code -> infra/DevOps -> tests
The affected files table must include: file path, change type (create/modify/extend), and a description of the change
Include a Mermaid architecture diagram if the change involves multiple components or services

read: memory.json (work item details and codebase analysis from previous steps)

bestPractices: Describe the 'what' and 'why', never the 'how' — no code, no pseudocode, no implementation details
Use business-domain language throughout: feature names, entity names, workflow names
Ensure every acceptance criterion maps to at least one implementation task
Order tasks so each one can be completed without depending on a later task
Keep the verification checklist actionable — each item should be testable with a yes/no answer
Include both positive and negative test scenarios in the testing strategy
If the change is simple (single file, config-only), skip the architecture diagram

substeps.name: Read work item details and codebase analysis from memory
substeps.description: Load all context from previous steps needed to generate the plan
actions: Read memory.json to get workItem from fetch-work-item step
Read memory.json to get codebaseAnalysis from analyze-codebase step
Verify both are present — if either is missing, report error and stop
Identify the acceptance criteria that drive the plan structure

substeps.name: Generate implementation plan
substeps.description: Create the full implementation plan with all required sections
actions: Section 1 — Summary and acceptance criteria: Summarize the work item purpose in 2-3 sentences. List all acceptance criteria verbatim from the work item.

Section 2 — Prerequisites and dependencies: List external dependencies, required permissions, environment setup, and prerequisite knowledge. Include any blocking items that must be resolved before implementation.

Section 3 — Affected files table: Create a table with columns: File Path, Change Type (create/modify/extend), Description. Populate from codebaseAnalysis.filesToCreate and filesToModify. Order by dependency layer: config -> models -> services -> controllers -> infra -> tests.

Section 4 — Step-by-step implementation tasks: Break the work into ordered tasks. Follow the ordering: dependencies/config -> module wiring -> feature code -> infra/DevOps -> tests. Each task describes WHAT to do in business-domain terms, not HOW to code it. Map each task to the acceptance criteria it fulfills.
Section 5 — Architecture diagram (Mermaid): If the change involves multiple components or services, include a Mermaid diagram showing the flow. Skip this section for simple/single-file changes.
Section 6 — Testing strategy: List test categories needed (unit, integration, e2e). Identify key positive and negative test scenarios. Note any test infrastructure or fixtures needed.

Section 7 — Verification checklist: Create a checklist of yes/no verifiable items. Include: all acceptance criteria met, no regressions in existing tests, code follows identified patterns, config/infra changes applied, documentation updated if needed.

substeps.name: Store plan in memory
substeps.description: Write the complete implementation plan to memory.json
actions: Write implementationPlan object to current step's informationProduced section
Include all sections: summary, acceptanceCriteria, prerequisites, affectedFiles, tasks, architectureDiagram (if applicable), testingStrategy, verificationChecklist
Note any assumptions or open questions under Notes

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for any user interactions?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?
Verify: Plan contains NO code snippets — only describes what to implement
Verify: Business-domain names used throughout, not technical/infrastructure names
Verify: Task ordering follows dependencies/config -> module wiring -> feature code -> infra/DevOps -> tests
Verify: Every acceptance criterion maps to at least one task
Output: 'Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Linear flow: Read work item and codebase analysis from memory -> Generate complete implementation plan with all 7 sections -> Store plan in memory -> Compliance check. Approval is handled at the template level, not within this step.

memoryFileUsage.readFrom: Previous steps (workItem from fetch-work-item, codebaseAnalysis from analyze-codebase)
fields: Information Produced: implementationPlan object with summary, acceptanceCriteria, prerequisites, affectedFiles, tasks, architectureDiagram, testingStrategy, verificationChecklist
Decisions Made: Task ordering, section inclusion/exclusion (e.g., architecture diagram)
Notes: Assumptions, open questions, areas needing clarification

summary.description: 2-3 sentence summary of the work item purpose plus verbatim acceptance criteria

prerequisites.description: External dependencies, permissions, environment setup, blocking items

affectedFiles.description: Table of file paths with change type and description, ordered by dependency layer
affectedFiles.ordering: config -> models -> services -> controllers -> infra -> tests

tasks.description: Ordered implementation tasks in business-domain language
tasks.ordering: dependencies/config -> module wiring -> feature code -> infra/DevOps -> tests
rules: Map each task to acceptance criteria

architectureDiagram.conditional: Include only for multi-component or multi-service changes

testingStrategy.description: Test categories, key scenarios (positive and negative), test infrastructure needs

verificationChecklist.description: Yes/no verifiable items covering acceptance criteria, regressions, patterns, config, and docs

keyRules: No code snippets — describe WHAT to implement, not the implementation
Use business-domain names, not technical/infrastructure names
Step ordering: dependencies/config -> module wiring -> feature code -> infra/DevOps -> tests
